help.roadBody: Follow the road of lanterns onward. Fight monsters, gather cards, relics and phials, and defeat the boss of each of the {count} acts. Unlit lanterns hide what they hold — but pay a bounty for the walking.
help.combatBody: Each turn you draw 5 cards and gain 3 Energy (⬤). Play a card by clicking or dragging — attacks need a target when several enemies remain. Enemies telegraph their intent above their heads.
help.firesBody: Rest sites heal 30% or upgrade a card. Shops sell cards, relics, phials — and can remove a card from your deck. Keep your deck lean; every reward is optional.
help.glassBody: Every creature is glass with a row of Facets under its lifebar. Attacks that draw unblocked blood chip a facet (heavy cards chip more). Fill the gauge and the glass SHATTERS: it loses its next action, is Cracked, and spills Embers into your lantern. Time a shatter to deny the blow you can't survive.
help.lanternBody: Embers fuel your Lantern Art — one signature power, always available, once a turn (press A). Drag any card onto the lantern to kindle it: the card burns away and feeds the lantern 1 ember. Once a turn; curses refuse the fire.
help.title: How to Play
help.vigilBody: Nothing is wasted. At the start of each run the Keeper offers a boon and lets you choose your Lantern Art. When you fall, carve one thing into the stone — a monument your next run can recover in that same act. Every shatter, kindle and slaying feeds lifetime Deeds that unlock new cards, relics, and a second aspect, the Ashwarden. Reach the dawn once and the Vows open: an optional difficulty ladder for those who'd walk a crueler road.
help.vigilTitle: The Vigil — What Death Leaves Behind
help.wardBody: Ward is held light that absorbs damage but expires each turn. Cracked ×1.5 damage taken · Dimmed −25% damage dealt · Brittle −25% Ward · Smolder burns each turn, and leaps to another enemy when its host dies or shatters.

eighthOmen.resolved: THE EIGHTH OMEN WAS NEVER AN OMEN. IT WAS THE SHADOW OF A DOOR.

hollowLamplighter.inscription: Pay the Hollow Lamplighter five prices along the Unlit Way.

meetings.ask: Your lantern is noisy. Give me the next three embers it catches.
meetings.cannot: Promise the embers now. The lantern will pay before you do.
meetings.paid: Six panes were carried away from a window no wall could hold.

meetings.ask: Gold remembers every hand. Let one hundred and sixty pieces forget yours.
meetings.cannot: Your purse is warm, but not warm enough.
meetings.paid: The Pale Ones watch the paths that point beyond the crown.

meetings.ask: The road counts the vessel. Give me twelve measures of yours.
meetings.cannot: I will not hollow you below thirty. Return with a larger vessel.
meetings.paid: Your forebears died standing, facing east.

meetings.cannot: You have spent the gift already. Bring me one that is still yours.
meetings.paid: The empty lantern is the token that purchases an audience with the mask.

meetings.ask: Last price: leave this lantern with one heartbeat. The rest belongs to the dark.
meetings.cannot: One heartbeat is enough. Refusal is the only poverty left.
meetings.paid: Light the panes. The door will know you.

hollowLamplighter.name: The Hollow Lamplighter

ownShade.final: We were never walking to be free. We were carrying light to the lock.
fragments: I remember the stone. You walked away before I stopped calling.
You have left a shape behind. The road has learned to keep us.
I have seen it. Beyond the Sovereign there is no dawn — only a door pretending to be one.
ownShade.inscription: Defeat the self that still remembers the road. Three shades must go out.
ownShade.name: Your Own Shade

paleOnes.huntInscription: Defeat three pale foes and follow the cold motes they leave behind.
paleOnes.inscription: Hunt the Pale Ones. Gather nine motes from glass that has forgotten colour.
paleOnes.name: The Pale Ones
progress: The first pale mote chills the lantern.

unreadablePage.inscription: Win five dawns carrying the Unreadable Page.
unreadablePage.name: The Unreadable Page
pages: FIRST PAGE — Six panes were cut from one fire, then scattered before the first Vigil.
SECOND PAGE — Pale figures carried the shards west, so the thing beyond the door could not follow.
THIRD PAGE — A pilgrim died standing. Where he stopped, the road did not.
FOURTH PAGE — The Sovereign took an empty lantern and wore a king's shape over the lock.
FIFTH PAGE — The Rose Window is a map, not a memorial. Light it, then look beyond the crown.

usurper.bought: Now the throne knows what you carry.
usurper.death: The mask is broken. Look beyond the crown.
usurper.inscription: Carry the lantern with no flame to the sealed door, and unmask the Usurper.
usurper.itemText: Cold glass. No wick. The merchant will not say who left it.
usurper.name: The Usurper
usurper.poor: Cold goods, warm price. Come back carrying a dawn's worth of gold.

ownShade1.deathDialogue: I remember the stone. You walked away before I stopped calling.
ownShade1.name: The Shade That Fell

ownShade2.deathDialogue: You have left a shape behind. The road has learned to keep us.
ownShade2.name: The Shade That Returned

ownShade3.deathDialogue: I have seen it. Beyond the Sovereign there is no dawn — only a door pretending to be one.
ownShade3.name: The Shade That Remembers

dialogue: {aspect}. At last, the lantern brings me a name.
The Sovereign was a mask. You have paid to meet the face beneath it.
Break me, and the empty lantern will remember fire.

whispers: There is a colour the road refuses to name.
A pale hand has touched the dark side of the glass.
Six spaces wait where no window stands.
The dead walk twice: once in flesh, once in memory.
A lantern without flame is still a key.
Count the panes that do not catch the dawn.
A page can be read only after it survives the dawn.
The eighth sign is not written among the seven.
The gaunt keeper remembers the road you did not take.
Pale motes gather like frost around a hidden seam.
Your monument does not always lie down.
The merchant keeps one cold thing beneath the counter.
Broken glyphs are the shadow of a complete sentence.
Five pages make a chapter; five prices make a confession.
Three deaths will teach your shade to speak plainly.
The Vigil has a window, though no wall holds it.
Each shard lights one pane of the Rose Window.
The Pale Ones are not hunting you. They are pointing east.
The Sovereign is a mask worn before the last door.
When six panes burn, look beyond the crown.
There is a sealed door beyond the crown.
Its inscription has waited longer than the Vigil.
Bring six shards to the Rose Window.
The pilgrimage continues.

b1.l2: Take your time. The road isn't going anywhere.

b2.l1: Take this. Those before you left it behind; now it's yours.
b2.l2: The road runs east. At its end stands a sealed door. Bring back the six shards of emberglass, and it will open.
b2.l3: Beyond it, they say, lies the Gilded City. Reach it, and you will be home.

b3.l1: You take up the lantern and step out. The long road runs east, and the sky is not yet light.
b3.l2: Behind you, the fire is still burning.

pre.l1: An old man sits by the road, holding a lantern. There is no flame in it.
pre.l2: Your lantern burns too full. I have seen plenty like you.

post.l1: Oil can be shared. Flame cannot. Flame you carry to the end yourself.
post.l2: He gathers the three embers into the hollow lantern. The lantern does not light.

pre.l1: Farther east along the Unlit Way, the old man is waiting again, the hollow lantern set before him.
pre.l2: Last time — that was you. Three embers, not one short. I remember these hands.
pre.l3: Thinner, these hands. The road feeds no one well.

post.l1: He counts the coins one by one, and does not pocket them. He lays them out along the road, piece by piece, pointing east.

pre.l1: This time the old man is on his feet, waiting. Until he has looked you full in the face, he does not speak.
pre.l2: Stand closer. Raise your lantern — let me see this face properly.
pre.l3: A scar on your brow. Last time there was none. …The road gives them out. Naturally.

post.l1: Don't look at me like that. An old man tells what he has seen — no more than that.
post.l2: He steps back and looks you over once more — from the face down to the boots.

pre.l1: The old man's eyes go past you, to the things you carry, counting them one by one.
pre.l2: Things from the western fire — I know them at a glance. All these years, the make has never changed.
pre.l3: Give me one answer, that is all. Last time, standing where you stand — was that you?
pre.l4: Before you can make a sound, he waves the question away — as if he would rather not learn where it leads.

post.l1: He puts the gift away. The hollow lantern sits by his feet, dark as ever.
post.l2: The next stretch is long. Spend yourself slow.

pre.l1: Where the Unlit Way runs out, the old man stands in the middle of the road, hollow lantern raised. He does not let you pass.
pre.l2: The last price. Past me, no one on this road will ask anything more of you.
pre.l3: A lifetime under this lamp, learning the ones who pass. The faces I know. The people I was never sure of.

post.l1: Go. I have seen many off along this stretch.
post.l2: He steps aside and lifts the hollow lantern toward the east, as if to light the way. There is no light in it. He lifts it all the same.
post.l3: If you meet another out there who carries a lamp — look close at the face, for me.

paleOnes.p1: The first mote settles into the Lens, cold as frost. The Pale Ones do not hunt you; they stand facing east, and that is all. The Vigil records it: someone had already walked this stretch as far as here.
paleOnes.p2: The Lens fills. Every mote is what someone had left when there was nothing else to spend. You are not counting kills. You are counting the places where other people ended.
paleOnes.done: Nine gathered; the Lens stops chilling. One pane of the Rose Window answers. That light is not new. It is light someone carried, and did not carry as far as the door.

ownShade.p1: The first shade goes out. It knew you. It called after you, and you did not stop. Where it went out, nothing was left on the ground: a shade is only memory.
ownShade.p2: The second shade goes out. The broken sentences come clearer each time, as though someone were finally learning to speak plainly. The more you put out, the quieter the road gets.
ownShade.done: The third shade goes out and a pane answers. The Vigil sets it down: what you put out was the part of you that still remembered how to walk. You will set out just the same. Nothing on the road will call your name now.

usurper.p1: The lantern with no flame changes hands. Cold glass; a wick that has never burned. The merchant will not say who left it — only that things of this kind always come back west on their own.
usurper.done: The mask breaks; the throne does not empty. You pass him, and he goes on sitting, waiting for the next one to reach the door. What you beat was a refusal, not a man.

eighthOmen.p1: The eighth omen rises. The book lists seven; the eighth is not in the book. It lies across the road too squarely for an omen — more like the shadow of something shut.
eighthOmen.done: Dawn comes and the omen is still there. It never was an omen. It is the shadow of a door — and a shadow reaching this far means the door has been there all along, and shut all along.

unreadablePage.p1: The first page comes clear: six panes cut from one fire and scattered before the first Vigil. The Vigil adds a line of its own: whoever wrote that was not there.
unreadablePage.p2: Second page: pale figures carried the shards west, so that what lay beyond the door could not follow. The carrying is true. The reason is the page's own.
unreadablePage.p3: Third page: a pilgrim died standing, and where he stopped, the road did not. It is the shortest page and the barest — written flat, the way a man writes what he watched.
unreadablePage.p4: Fourth page: the Sovereign took an empty lantern and wore a king's shape over the lock. The Vigil sets it down: under that crown there is a lock, not a head.
unreadablePage.done: All five read. The fifth says the Rose Window is a map, not a memorial. It does not say what the map is of. The more of it you light, the less it looks like a window.

hollowLamplighter.p1: Three embers into the hollow lantern; it does not light. The old man lifts it and studies — not the lamp, you. First meeting: what he checks is the face.
hollowLamplighter.p2: A hundred and sixty coins leave your hand. He pockets none of them; he lays them along the road, facing east — the way a man counts something that is already standing in line.
hollowLamplighter.p3: Twelve measures of you, handed over. He looks at the scar first and the face second, then explains the mismatch away himself. Honest men do that. Everything he sees is right; everything he concludes is wrong.
hollowLamplighter.p4: The Keeper's gift passes to the old man. He knows the make; he says it has not changed in all these years. Then he stops. He waves the rest of it off before it can get anywhere.
hollowLamplighter.done: The last price paid: one heartbeat left in the lantern. The old man stands aside and lifts the hollow lamp toward the east — there is no light in it; he lifts it all the same. A pane answers. He looks at you the way a man looks at a face he has spent his life checking.

pane.1: One pane lights; five stay dark. One pane is not a window yet — only a bright point in the dark.
pane.2: Two panes now. The window starts to have a shape. The lit places are not random; they read as places that were kept.
pane.3: Three: half. At half, the glass begins to hold a reflection. You step closer, and the thing in the window steps closer too.
pane.4: Four lit, and the hearth is warmer than it was. The longer you look at that window, the less it looks like something built for looking out of.
pane.5: Five lit; one short. The light no longer keeps to its own panes. It runs together, the way a thing that was once whole runs together. The last shard is still out on the road.

b1.l1: The sixth shard goes back into the window.
b1.l2: Six panes, none missing. In the window, the fire is one thing again.
b1.l3: The light does not pass through.

b2.l1: Lit to the last pane, the window stops being a window.
b2.l3: Then you see that there is another one behind you.

b3.l1: A single line of them, from one edge of the window to the other.
b3.l2: Every one of them is you, and every one of them has a point of light at his breast.
b3.l3: There are as many of them as the times you have set out.
b3.l4: Every time the fire was rekindled, a real one of you went out through that door. You have never once set out.

b4.l1: Along the road, the monuments move at once. They were never memorials. Each is a walker who died on his feet and did not lie down, because he was waiting for the door.
b4.l2: They straighten, they form up, they push. The door knows two things: those who have walked, and one whole fire. Every one of them has walked.
b4.l3: You did not open the door.

b1.l1: The door still stands open. The ones who pushed it are still standing on both sides of it. You go in.
You step in through the window. Its far side is the far side of the door.
b1.l2: On this side the hearthlight runs backwards: every step forward is brighter than the last.
b1.l3: It is the same road. You are walking it back from the far end.

b1.l1: We have been standing on this side all along. You have looked at it many times; you have never stood on it.
b1.l2: You know the road. You have only ever known it from the other side.

b1.l1: The king is still sitting. We went past him, and not one of us ever sat down.
b1.l2: Broken haloes are still ringing on this side. When we went by, not one of us turned round.

b1.l1: The city is still waiting. We stopped waiting; that is why we are here.
b1.l2: That light down in the water is not a lamp. It is not one on this side either.

b1.l1: This is where the monuments stand thickest. The ones who stopped earliest ended up nearest the fire.
b1.l2: The ash is what they burned down to. The trees grew on it, and the road you walk was laid with their strength.
b1.l3: The paired lamps are still burning. Whoever lit them did not get far. He is standing right under them.
b1.l4: No one stops you. The monuments stand aside, as though the middle had been kept clear for this one crossing all along.
b1.l5: It is the longest stretch and the quietest. You can sit here a while. They can afford to wait.

b1.l1: You've arrived. You know this place.
b1.l2: I never lied to you. I only never said who it was that went out.
b1.l3: Every time the fire tore you, the part that would not go stayed here. Enough of it stayed to make a face. This one.
b1.l4: Sit down. Let one of them do the walking; that is all this has ever been.

b1.l1: The six are one fire again, and the Queue has arrived.
b1.l2: This time there is no half to leave behind. The fire does not tear you: there is nowhere left for the fear to stand.

b2.l1: The door is ahead. The first one ever to get this far sat down one step short of it.
b2.l4: That step was yours. No one walked it for you.

b1.l1: The door stands open. One after another the same figure goes through, in the order they stopped.
b1.l2: You are the last of them. The whole Queue has arrived.
b1.l3: Inside the gate there is a fire that knows you. To arrive is to come home.

b1.l1: This one did not come back either.
b1.l2: The door closes again. The six panes stay lit, and the Queue is one longer. The fire in the west goes on burning, waiting for someone to sit down at it again.

event-mirror.c0: The mirror shows the card twice. You can carry one away. The other stays in the glass, as if someone were keeping it for you.
event-mirror.c1: The glass breaks. The same reflection lies scattered across every piece, still smiling. You pick one thing out of the wreck that you no longer want to carry, and blood runs down your fingers.
event-mirror.c2: You turn away. The one in the glass turns half a breath later, then watches you the whole way out.
event-mirror.coda: There is more than one mirror on this road, and every one of them is half a breath behind you.

event-woundedKnight.c0: You stop the bleeding. He presses the relic into your hand, gets himself upright against the pillar, and says he only wants to get a little further.
event-woundedKnight.c1: You take what the gauntlet is holding. He does not fight you, and he does not go down. Behind the crushed visor the breathing slows, and stops.
event-woundedKnight.c2: You leave. One look back: still against the pillar, still on his feet.
event-woundedKnight.coda: The next time you come by, there is a monument at the foot of the pillar.

event-library.c0: Among the waterlogged pages you find one still legible. It was written by someone who lived here, and all of it is about what they would do on the day the door opened.
event-library.c1: You sit down among the stacks. The water noise falls back; your breathing slows. If this city is short of anything, it is not places to sit and wait.
event-library.coda: They wrote their waiting until it filled a library. Not one page of it is about setting out.

event-fleshTrader.c0: You hand over a piece of yourself for a relic. He takes it without fuss, like a man who has done this many times.
event-fleshTrader.c1: You refuse. He does not press it. The long fingers close. "Next time," he says, like a man who already knows there will be one.
event-fleshTrader.coda: He never chases a price. He has seen enough: none of the ones who go east come back — and there is always another going east.

event-forgottenShrine.c0: At the shrine you set down one thing you no longer want to carry. The thing inside the stone watches, and gives you nothing back. Prayer is not what it is waiting for.
event-forgottenShrine.c1: You sweep the bone and silver offerings into your pack. The thing inside the stone does not move. It only makes a note.
event-forgottenShrine.c2: You step back and turn. The hum goes on as before. It has hummed for years past counting; it is not short of one more visitor.
event-forgottenShrine.coda: The moss grows back over the offerings. This shrine has taken more than it ever promised.
